post.description: Starts a goal's curriculum (skill graph, plan and course outlines) or, for an explain question, its quick explanation again, such as after a start failed. A run already going is joined, and only what is missing is written. POST /goals starts it the first time. Stream GET /generations/{generationId}/events for live steps: a curriculum reports `understandGoal`, `readExamNotice` (only while research reads a class test's own material before its skill graph), `buildSkillGraph`, `saveSkills`, `preparePlacement` (placement's questions start being written, by a run of their own that this stream doesn't follow: GET /goals/{goalId}/placement asks each once it's written), `createPlan`, `outlineCourses`, `prepareFirstLessons`, then `goalReady`, or `workflowError` when the plan couldn't be built; an explanation `classifyQuestion`, `findExplanation`, `writeExplanation` (completed once the explanation can be read), then `explanationReady` once its course to go further is linked. A run that finds another run already writing the goal reports `joinRunningGoal` or `joinRunningExplanation` with that run's id as `entityId`: follow that run's events instead. Starting a goal whose plan is already built again with a newer `researchId` reconciles the plan with that research, which counts as small AI help: a refusal is `SLOW_DOWN` or `USAGE_LIMIT_REACHED` (403 asks a guest to sign up, 402 a free learner to upgrade or come back, 429 Plus to slow down).

Prepares content around one of the learner's study sessions: every lesson of this session and the next gets written in the background. Block starts, stops and the last block's completion call it themselves; call it when the learner moves a session along another way, never on a screen view. For a guest only the lesson they reach next is written, counted as its start like opening it.

Starts a Library course as the learner's goal, with nothing to type or confirm: a learn goal on the course (a language goal for a language course, or an exam goal for a course linked to a public exam blueprint) whose plan is built from the course's outline right away, its level bands as phases, starting at `chapterId` when one is sent (the chapters before it are left out). Onboarding (GET /goals/{goalId}/onboarding) then asks the level, an optional date, and the learner's time, and places them (a language's level test); a chapter start skips the level and placement. The optional `targetDate` sets a deadline; explicit null skips the date, while an omitted date defaults to the linked exam's next stored date when available. A new goal's run starts writing ahead what its plan needs (placement's questions, the first lessons); follow it through the onboarding's `generationId`, or POST /goals/{goalId}/generations when it didn't start. A course nobody outlined yet gets its plan from that run. It counts against the plan's goal limits (429 GOAL_LIMIT_REACHED or SLOW_DOWN, or 403 SIGN_UP_REQUIRED for a guest once the day's AI budget all guests share is spent); the learner's active goal already on the course comes back instead (200). Published public courses, and the learner's own private ones. Guests can start one.

post.description: Claims a pending or failed question and returns one grounded answer as an AI SDK UI message stream, whatever the question is about (a lesson, chapter, plan or mock). `lessonId` in the question routes is a Library lesson. A first question about a lesson screen that someone already asked there streams the saved shared answer right away, without counting against the allowance or reading memory. Otherwise the answer counts against the learner's tutor allowance (403 asks a guest to sign up, 402 a free learner to upgrade, 429 to slow down or come back after the limit resets, with `SLOW_DOWN` or `USAGE_LIMIT_REACHED` and details), and reads the learner's memory. Its `finish` event comes once the answer is saved, so the answer is done and the learner can ask again; a `data-memory` part may follow with what the exchange changed in memory (each change's `action`, `fact` and `previous` with `id` and `statement`), to show and undo with `POST /v1/me/memory/change-reversals`. In a goal's conversation with the buddy, a `data-plan-change` part carries the plan change the answer proposed (a `PlanChange` waiting for the learner's OK) as soon as it's saved; the question's `planChange` holds it too. A `data-plan-changes-replaced` part follows it with the `ids` of earlier proposals it replaced because it changes the same thing (their status is now `replaced`). When the buddy only acted (a plan change or an app tool) and wrote nothing, the answer is a short confirmation of what it put under it. The streamed text is provisional: right before `finish`, a `data-saved-answer` part carries the answer as it was saved (`answer`), its links checked, and replaces it. Only that text and answers read back from the questions routes link anything: a buddy answer links only the in-app paths of the web app it was given (pages such as `/today` or `/plan`, `/session?block={id}` for one of today's blocks, `/challenge/{planItemId}`), and the lesson tutor's only web addresses; render links from the streamed text as plain words.

section.description: As a syllabus subject's `areas` name it, such as Matemática

weight.description: Its normalized share of the exam score when exam shares are available, otherwise its share of the goal's skill importance. Sections outside an available exam share map count as zero; set-aside sections are excluded before normalization

sections.description: Preparation in each section of the goal's skill graph, by the goal's rule on its own skills and answers with the goal's tests, which span every section: weighted by `weight`, they are `value`. Subjects the learner removed are excluded, including skills from finished lessons. Subjects left out for time, past basics or skipped bases still count. stage.description: The value's stage, capped at growing until the goal's globally heaviest skills have the evidence Solid needs (`components.coverage.heaviest` with the goal's quality evidence). It can stay growing at a value of 0.75 or more; use this stage rather than inferring Solid from the number

status.description: Null while nothing is scheduled

value.description: Preparation: coverage times how well the studied part is known, in each section (`sections`), weighted by its normalized exam share when available, otherwise its skill importance. It sits within its contributing subjects, or is zero when none contributes. An exam goal's one number; other goals read their progress in lessons (the syllabus's `lessons`)

weekGain.description: Preparation gained since the start of the learner's week (Monday, in their time zone)

heaviest.description: The goal's globally heavier part (its hardest and most asked skills) and the share of it studied. Solid eligibility uses this goal-level coverage with the goal's quality evidence; it caps `stage`, never the weighted `value`

value.description: Share of the goal studied, each skill counting by the exam's weight on it and how hard it is

evidence.description: How many answers the weighted ones are worth as evidence

supported.description: The share right the answers support (Wilson's lower bound), the value to show for this part. Preparation counts each section's own, from its answers

value.description: Accuracy on questions never seen before, each answer counting by its skill's importance. Null until a section has the few answers mastery needs: show that it comes after a few practice questions

mastery.description: Read from the answers in positively weighted sections (`sections`) with enough of them to count mastery: a few answers spread over many subjects count in none yet, and zero-weight sections do not contribute

kind.description: fullReviews: an exam goal whose plan has no mock exams (free) counts its full reviews in the exam's format (study blocks with `fullReview`), which its plan gives it on the mock's day

plusRequired.description: The test needs Plus now: the plan has no mocks and its free days are over. Show the mock with the Plus mark

mocks.description: The fourth part: an exam goal's mock exams (or its full reviews when its plan has no mocks), or another goal's weekly challenges (it has no exam to rehearse). Preparation stays under 75% until one is taken, never for a test the learner's plan can't take

value.description: How much of what was studied is still remembered

days.description: Days of extra time that catch up; 0 when lessons says it instead

lessons.description: Lessons earlier days left that the learner hasn't caught up on: they come first in the plan, and the learner is behind until they're done. Say this count instead of days when present

challenges.description: The phases' challenges left to win

Exams still wait for their mocks and reviews. Never say it finished while required challenges remain; say how many are left

Every lesson of the plan is studied or tested out and every required phase challenge won. Free language call challenges can remain pending and locked, with no won result. Non-exam reviews remain practice after finishing and never delay this status. An exam also waits for its mocks and reviews still ahead

lessons.description: The lessons left, to do or set aside when the date came

due.description: When the next review is due

example.description: A worked example: the back of the study card

fading.description: Memory has dropped below the retention reviews aim for

recallDays.description: Different days the skill was remembered

chapterId.description: A chapter whose lesson is written just in time

extra.description: A "10 more minutes" block after the day's session

fullReview.description: A full review: every topic, in place of a mock the plan doesn't have

mistakesOnly.description: A practice block that only fixes the learner's mistakes (their drills, no practice questions): name it for that, not as mixed practice

netScored.description: Practice scored net (a wrong answer cancels a right one, as in Cebraspe exams): statements can be answered with dontKnow to leave them blank. Swipe capsules are scored net on their own

oftenTested.description: An exam topic the board asks a lot in past papers: tiles tag it Often tested

planItemKey.description: Logical plan work identity; never a database UUID

reinforcement.description: A short lesson before a boss rematch

subject.description: The goal's subject the block studies, by its short name (as `GET /v1/goals/{goalId}/syllabus` names it): label the block with it. Null for blocks that mix subjects, and for goals with fewer than two subjects

waitReason.description: Why a phase challenge waits: earlier lessons or an earlier phase challenge in this session are still pending or active. Completed or skipped work releases it. Null for blocks that can open in any order, including lessons, review, practice, the weekly challenge and mocks

weakest.description: A review of the learner's weakest studied topics, none of them due: a day with nothing due and nothing else to study gets it instead of staying empty. Say so rather than calling it due

dueToday.description: Skills due for review today (time capsules)

section.description: The course or exam subject the chapter's skills belong to; null when the goal's graph names none

groups.description: Every skill of the goal as a card, grouped by chapter in plan order, with each section's chapters together (show a section header when there are two or more)

description.description: The front of the card: the idea

example.description: The back of the card: an example

recallDays.description: Different days it was remembered; Mastered at three

open.description: Open entries in the mistakes notebook

preparation.description: Null for a quick explanation: one answer, not a goal to prepare for

left.description: The area's skills still below their bar, in plan order

minutes.description: Study time the plan still gives these skills at the learner's pace, reviews included

total.description: The area's skills in the goal

rule.description: `solid`: every skill must be Solid. `examWeighted`: skills with an exam weight of 4 or 5 must be Solid, the rest at least Learning

stillNeeded.description: "Still needed to reach your goal": the goal's skills below their bar by area (chapter, or plan phase before chapters exist), with the plan's time for them. Areas already at the bar have nothing left

options.description: Answer with the chosen option's index, or indexes

question.description: The statement to judge true or false

BankQuestion.description: A bank question without its answers

NothingToSkip.description: No lessons remain for a test-out to skip. Open the chapter instead.

ceremony.description: The one milestone the learner hasn't been shown yet (a belt this work crossed, new glasses): show it as a full-screen moment before the result, then mark it shown; null when there's none

energy.description: The tenth of Energy its answers reached going up (60, 80, 100)

level.description: The belt level its Brain Power reached, the day's bonus included

reached.description: The belt level and the tenth of Energy this work took the learner to, to celebrate on its result; nothing on a repeat, which celebrates none of it again

changeId.description: The plan change that skipped the lessons; undo it through the goal's plan changes. Null when nothing was skipped or the plan isn't built yet.

lessonsSkipped.description: The lessons it skipped, the count its plan change says: a topic still being written counts the lessons the plan teaches in its place

status.description: `ready`: GET the test-out now. `generating`: follow the run's stream until `testOutQuestionsReady`

lessonsSkipped.description: The lessons its result said were off the plan

undone.description: The learner undid the skip: its lessons are back in the plan

complete.description: Every area of every phase has a confident starting point. False while the plan has no skills yet

dayBudgetSpent.description: How much of today's few minutes the day's answers used, from 0 to 1: the further along of its two limits, the answers and the answering time. dayBudgetUsed.description: Today's few minutes of placement are used: no next question today; the first week's sessions ask the rest

started.description: This goal's placement already has answers: a client coming back resumes at `next` instead of showing placement's start

area.description: The plan's area: the course or exam subject the skill graph put its skills in, as plan focus names it. Null when the plan names none

startSkillId.description: The area's first skill the learner can't do yet; null when all known

question.description: Answer in the learner's own words, as `text`

confident.description: Placement is at least 80% sure about this start

startSkillId.description: Null when the whole phase is known

PlacementStatus.description: What to do next. `preparing`: the goal's skill map isn't ready, so there's nothing to place yet; ask again soon. `asking`: `next` is the question to ask. `waitingForQuestions`: the questions placement needs next (`needsItems`) are still being written; ask again soon, or finish placement with what's known. `done`: nothing more to ask now, because every start is confident (`complete`), today's few minutes are used (`dayBudgetUsed`), or no question exists for what's left, which lessons and reviews settle instead. `unavailable`: no placement question could be written and none was answered; finish placement and go on without it (the first week's sessions and lessons place the learner). `failed`: the run building the goal's plan gave up before it had skills; start it again with POST /goals/{goalId}/generations.

complete.description: Every area of every phase had a confident start when placement finished. False when the plan had no skills yet: nothing was placed

dailyMinutes.description: The day's total across active goals

goals.description: The main goal first, then the rest oldest first

kind.description: curriculum: skill graph, plan and outlines for learn, exam and language goals; explanation: the quick explanation of an explain question

generations.description: What is being written for each new goal: stream GET /generations/{generationId}/events for live progress

index.description: The refused goal's place in the request

refused.description: Goals the learner's plan didn't allow; the others were created

research.description: Research started for exam and learn goals: poll GET /research/{researchId}

resource.description: What ran out, such as goal or activeGoals

change.description: The plan change a new time or date made

position.description: Its number in `subject`, as the subject's page lists it (`SyllabusChapter.position`); its number in the plan when `subject` is null

subject.description: The subject or module whose page numbers it (Biologia · Chapter 4); null when the goal's subjects have no pages (a plan from one course, a language) or none lists it

key.description: The subject's key in the goal's syllabus

open.description: Open mistakes on the chapter's skills, including today's entries; correction availability comes from the mistakes notebook and its practice capability

skills.description: The chapter's map, in plan order

summaries.description: Summary cards of the chapter's finished lessons, in lesson order

available.description: Offer the test while the chapter has lessons left, unless it was failed today without a lesson studied in it since; it becomes available again on the next learner-local day

plusRequired.description: A free exam plan past its first week takes the chapter's test-out with Plus only: show it marked Plus; its endpoints answer 402

skillIds.description: Skills it teaches, so tapping a skill on the map lists its lessons

written.description: Its screens are written, so opening it starts no writing and apps may load it ahead

fading.description: Its chance of recall dropped: a review relights it

prerequisiteIds.description: Skills of the goal learned before this one: the map's links

retrievability.description: The chance of recalling it now; null when never studied

courses.description: The courses the chapters come from, for the map's course view

emphasized.description: The goal is to refresh what the learner knew: lead with this

skills.description: Skills fading now, most faded first

refresh.description: Refresh mode: what's fading, which `refresh-practice` brings back

areaId.description: The chapter's id, or `phase:N` for skills not in a chapter yet

chapterId.description: Null before the skills have a chapter

courseId.description: The course the chapter belongs to

current.description: The learner is here: the plan's next lesson

brandSlug.description: With `courseSlug`, the course's public page; null for private courses

levels.description: Overview to Advanced; empty for private courses, which have no levels

nextLevel.description: The level after the plan's highest one; null at the top

planChapterCount.description: The course's chapters the plan uses

chapterCount.description: Chapters the course has at this level so far

inPlan.description: The plan teaches chapters from this level

nextLevel.description: The next level of the plan's course, which `POST /v1/goals/{goalId}/next-level` starts; null at the top

chapterCount.description: Chapters outlined at that level so far

related.description: Other public courses the plan drew from, to explore next

name.description: Empty for exam phases, which apps name by kind

state.description: The same state as the plan's phase (`GET /v1/goals/{goalId}/plan`). `current` is the earliest phase with work left, and none is once nothing of the plan is left; one before it is `done` once the learner finished its work, `unfinished` while some of it was set aside (missed days the plan couldn't fit back): never mark it done. `leftOut`: the plan holds none of its work (a date too near for its topics): say it's not in the plan, and leave it out of the phases counted done

courseWeights.description: How the learner's course weighs each of the exam's parts at their institution (an entrance exam's selection weights), as one source gives them; the plan gives the parts weighed more a bigger share of the time. fromMaterial.description: The subjects and topics come from the learner's own material (a class test's slides or notes), not an official notice

kind.description: `notice`: an exam whose notice lists its subjects and topics. `modules`: the plan's own areas

knownTopicsReturn.description: Where a `known` topic comes back to be confirmed: `practice`, or `reviews` for a free exam plan past its first week, whose practice is Plus (the quick review asks it then)

known.description: Of `done`, the ones skipped because the learner showed they know them, each counted once even when it shows in several subjects; the rest were studied

lessons.description: The lessons of the subjects in the plan (`notPlannedReason` null), added up: a goal that isn't an exam reads its progress as `done` of `total`, the same as its subjects' bars, so it reads 100% once every lesson of the plan is studied or known (with its phases' challenges won, the plan's status is then `finished`)

noticeUrl.description: The notice the subjects were read from

passMarks.description: What it takes to pass, as the notice says it; null when it doesn't

questionsSource.description: Where the subjects' `questions` come from when the notice gives none: the exam's latest edition, as one source counted it

subjects.description: The notice's subjects in its order (then areas the plan adds outside it), or the plan's modules in teaching order

topicsMapped.description: The plan says which skills teach which topic, so topics have a status

writtenPractice.description: When the exam's written tests are practiced, which the learner chooses on a written test's page (a subject whose `areas` include one of `parts`) and in the plan. Null for goals without written tests

areas.description: The plan's areas it gathers, as plan changes (`focusAreas`, `skipAreas`, `restoreAreas`) name them

chapters.description: Every chapter of the plan in this subject: the ones done, then in the order the plan studies them next

displayWeight.description: Normalized display weight among every notice subject, including written subjects not yet taught. Missing stated shares use the average stated subject. group.description: The notice's grouping, such as its basic knowledge part (P1)

imageUrl.description: The icon of the Library course the plan teaches it with

key.description: Stable within the goal's syllabus, URL-safe: the subject's page

lessonsDone.description: Its lessons the learner studied, never ones the plan set aside or they tested out of (`lessonsKnown`), so taking test-out credit back never lowers it

lessonsKnown.description: Its lessons the learner skipped because they showed they know them (tested out); a miss on one of those topics brings them back to study, lowering this, never `lessonsDone`. Show apart: "25 skipped because you know them"

lessonsTotal.description: Its size: the lessons the plan teaches in it, studied, known, to do or set aside (a plan without a date leaves out the ones the Library couldn't write), so finishing the plan reads 100%. Changing the learner's time or date changes what the plan holds, and so this; never `lessonsDone`

mastery.description: An exam subject's first answers to questions never seen before that say how well it's known, once it has the few its `preparation` needs to count mastery: show as "6 of 8 right". Null before, while its preparation counts no mastery yet: say it shows after a few practice questions. Null too whenever `preparation` is null

matrix.description: When the notice's syllabus for it is a skills matrix (ENEM's competencies and abilities) and its `topics` are the contents the matrix is paired with: the matrix's statements, word for word, as detail. Empty otherwise

name.description: The notice's own name for it, or the module's

nextDate.description: The next day the plan studies it; null once done or out of the plan

notPlannedReason.description: Why it isn't in the plan: `skipped` (the learner took the subject out; `restoreAreas` with its `areas` brings it back), `pastBasics` (a subject's basics the plan starts past: the learner said they know them, or does well in the subject with harder lessons), `skippedBase` (a base the learner chose to skip; `setBaseChoices` with `learn` brings it back), `time` (it doesn't fit before the deadline at the current pace), `missing` (no skill of the plan teaches it yet). Null when it's in the plan

Show it as the subject's number and bar, with `mastery` saying how much of it practice backs. A subject out of the plan (`notPlannedReason`) that the goal still counts (left out for time, its basics passed or its bases skipped, the exam testing it, with a section that weighs in the goal) has it too: show the number muted beside why it's out, with no bar. Null for other goals, whose subjects' progress is their lessons (`lessonsDone` and `lessonsKnown` of `lessonsTotal`), and for a subject out of the plan the goal doesn't count (`skipped` by the learner, `missing`, or weighing nothing in the goal)

questions.description: Questions on it in the exam, when the notice says

share.description: Its share of the exam: the notice's weight, or its share of the questions

shortName.description: A short label for it, for places with little room such as a lesson's subject

source.description: `notice`: a subject of the exam's notice. `plan`: a module of the plan, or an area the plan adds outside the notice

topicFrequencySource.description: Where how often the exam asks this subject's topics comes from, when the notice doesn't say and a source of its past papers does: the plan leaves out the topics asked least first. `basis` says what the source counted. Null otherwise

topics.description: The notice's topics in its own order; empty for modules

topicsKnown.description: Topics `known` (the learner showed they know them), shown apart from the ones studied; null when the plan doesn't map topics

topicsStudied.description: Topics `studied`; null when the plan doesn't map topics

chapterId.description: Its page is `GET /v1/goals/{goalId}/chapters/{chapterId}`; null while its lessons are still being written

known.description: Done only because the learner showed they know it: every lesson tested out, none studied. Say it was skipped, apart from the chapters done

nextDate.description: The next day the plan studies it; null once it's done

position.description: Its number in the subject, in the subject's order (the ones done first): every screen calls it Chapter 4

skillId.description: A `far` topic no chapter teaches yet: its skill, whose lesson plan is `GET /v1/goals/{goalId}/skills/{skillId}/outline` (POST `.../outline/generations` writes it now). state.description: `current` holds the plan's next lesson; at most one chapter has it

writing.description: A topic whose lessons aren't written yet (the plan writes them two weeks ahead). One starting after those weeks is `far`; any other's lessons are on the way

chapters.description: The chapters that teach it, in the subject's order; empty when `status` is null

frequency.description: How often past exams asked it, from a reading of past papers or a source that counted them (the subject's `topicFrequencySource` cites the latter): `high` is shown as "Appears a lot". Null when nothing says

heading.description: The heading the notice lists it under inside its subject, such as physics in ENEM's natural sciences: topics with the same heading come together, in order. Null when the subject has no headings

name.description: In the source's own words, as the notice lists it

nextDate.description: When the plan studies it next; null once studied or when unknown

notPlannedReason.description: Why it isn't in the plan: `skipped` (the learner took the subject out; `restoreAreas` with its `areas` brings it back), `pastBasics` (a subject's basics the plan starts past: the learner said they know them, or does well in the subject with harder lessons), `skippedBase` (a base the learner chose to skip; `setBaseChoices` with `learn` brings it back), `time` (it doesn't fit before the deadline at the current pace), `missing` (no skill of the plan teaches it yet). Null when it's in the plan

A topic whose lessons left were set aside after missed days is out for time (`notPlannedReason` `time`): `notPlanned`, or `inProgress` with the `chapters` the learner studied of it. Null when the plan doesn't say which skills teach which topic (plans made before topics were mapped): show the topic without a status

cadence.description: weekly (the default: spaced practice), biweekly (every other calendar week from the plan's first, and the final stretch) or finalWeeks (only the final weeks before the exam). Change it with a setWrittenCadence plan operation

finalWeeksFrom.description: The first day of the final weeks, when that choice applies; null when the plan has no date or is all final weeks, so finalWeeks isn't offered

parts.description: The written tests, as the plan's areas name them

freeUntil.description: Last day a free exam plan covers

freeWeekOver.description: A free exam plan past its first week: its new lessons, practice, challenges and mocks come with Plus, while reviews and fixing mistakes stay free

focusPart.description: The part of a focused area the learner named, such as biology and chemistry (`focusAreas` with `parts`); null when it's focused whole

partOf.description: The area it's part of, for an option the exam counts inside another subject (the foreign language a candidate takes, inside ENEM's languages area): show and focus it with that area, never on its own. Null for every other area

pastBasics.description: The learner said they're past its basics (`setAreaStart`)

reduced.description: The learner wants less of it (`reduceAreas`): it keeps its core, and its depth goes to other areas first

bases.description: The plan's bases to choose how to study; null when it has none

changes.description: Proposals first, then the last two weeks

course.description: The Library course the plan is built from, with its levels; null without one

end.description: Every lesson of the plan is studied or tested out and every required phase challenge won: time for what to study next (`GET /v1/goals/{goalId}/map`'s `next`, and POST `/v1/goals/{goalId}/next-level`). Free language plans can finish with their Plus call challenges still locked; those challenges retain their pending state, with no won result. Non-exam reviews remain practice after finishing; exams also wait for their mocks and reviews still ahead. Null while something required is left, lessons set aside included (a plan whose date came with lessons left isn't over: status `pastDate`) and required challenges too (status `challengesLeft`)

kind.description: Every lesson was studied or tested out and every required phase challenge won; Free language plans can finish with their Plus call challenges still locked

fullCourseEndDate.description: For an exam studying everything (`schedule.fullCourse`): `endDate`, when the learner finishes everything, once the plan holds all of it. Null otherwise, and while a few minutes a day leave some of it out even within the ten years a plan lays out

examChoices.description: The exam's choices (ENEM's foreign language: English or Spanish), each with its options and the one the learner takes (null until picked), which POST /v1/goals/{goalId}/plan/exam-choices changes; the plan studies only the picked options. Empty without choices

coreFits.description: Every topic (every skill's core) is in the plan, the ones worth more in more depth; false only when even the cores don't fit before the deadline

coveredShare.description: Share of everything, in depth, covered before the deadline (see measure)

deepensMostAsked.description: Most asked topics keep more depth

measure.description: exam: a share of the exam's questions and points; goal: of the goal's skills by weight

timeCovers.description: The learner's own daily time covers everything once the plan is planned again at it, even while `fits` is false (the plan holds less than their time fits): offer `fitOffer` at their time, never another daily time. False without a deadline

fitOffer.description: The lessons the learner's own time fits by the plan's date that the plan doesn't hold, as one change (`fitLessons`) with its effect, so Apply is one tap after its diff: offered once every lesson is done (no system refresh adds lessons then), or once the learner's time covers everything the plan leaves out (a date moved closer, then faster study). Send `operations` to POST /v1/goals/{goalId}/plan/changes as they are. Never offer less daily time as covering more. Null otherwise, and when it would add no lesson

fits.description: The plan with the change covers everything in depth by its date, as the change plans it: say so ("Your time covers everything by …") only then

requiresPlus.description: Free exam plans cover the first week and no mock exams

title.description: The lesson's title; for a skill whose lessons are still being written, its course's (empty when unknown or for the goal's own course: say "More lessons")

writing.description: A stand-in for a skill whose lessons are still being written; show it as being written, never by the skill's name

fundedMocks.description: Actual future todo mock items whose saved funding has started, with their real duration. Move them using the existing plan operation and item ID.

notice.description: An exam plan built before research read the exam's notice: reading while the reveal waits for that reading; usual once the wait ended without it (the plan follows the exam's usual structure and the reading arrives as a change to apply); null otherwise

ownLevel.description: The level the learner gave; null when they didn't say

ready.description: False while the planner is building the plan

fullCourse.description: The exam plan studies everything: what doesn't fit before the exam goes on after it (`setFullCourse`); the exam keeps its date. False for other goals, which study everything without a date

nextSitting.description: For a plan that goes on after its exam (`fullCourse`), whose mocks there are for the exam's next sitting: that sitting's first day, when the notice lists it; null otherwise

noSitting.description: An exam held several times a year with no sitting in the month of the learner's date; their date stays until they pick one. Null otherwise

closest.description: The first day of the closest sittings still open for registration, before and after `month`, each to offer with one tap (a setTargetDate change)

month.description: The first day of the learner's month

noticeDay.description: The exam day the notice gives when the plan counts down to another, to offer with one tap (a setTargetDate change); null otherwise

estimated.description: The likely day, while the edition's notice isn't out

targetDateEstimated.description: The date is the likely day of an exam whose notice isn't out yet

targetDateNamedMonth.description: The date is the start of the month the learner named, standing for that month: say the month, not the day

shortPlan.description: A test at most a week away, planned day by day: its study days and the day of its short mock; null for any other plan

mockDate.description: The short mock's day; null when the last day is a light review

lessonsStudied.description: Lessons of the plan the learner studied, not the ones placement skipped; ask how it's going only after the first

skippedActivities.description: Language practice left out of lessons; empty for other goals

tools.description: You'll use: the tools the plan's chapters use, essential first, with the learner's answer; empty when none do

studiedMinutes.description: Actual recorded study seconds this week, summed before rounding down to minutes

targetMinutes.description: The learner's shared weekly time budget across active goals, including past session targets. Exact minutes may be fractional; format them as a human duration for display.

weekTime.description: This week's study time against the learner's weekly budget, in the goal's week: the same numbers as Today's `week.time`

writtenPractice.description: When the exam's written tests (an essay, a discursive test) are practiced, which the learner chooses; the total practice stays the same. Null for plans without written tests and for a test days away

daysLeft.description: Days until the goal's date; null without one

knownCount.description: Bases placement or a test-out found the learner knows: they're out of the plan already. Say so

area.description: The plan's area, as plan changes name it

choice.description: deep: every lesson of it, core and depth; essential: its core, the first third of its lessons, before what builds on it (the default); quick: one short lesson that sums it up with a worked example; skip: none of it

choices.description: The choices it is open to, the only ones setBaseChoices accepts for it (others are refused with baseChoiceClosed): only deep once its core is studied (studied), and only when it has more than its core; every choice otherwise. Offer only these

minutes.description: What each way of studying it takes at the learner's pace

neededFor.description: What's built on it and worth more: an exam's notice topics, in the notice's own words, or a goal's outcome skills (its portfolio, its job search), the most valuable first

studied.description: The learner studied its core, none of its lessons still to do: say "Studied", and offer only deep study when choices has it

far.description: A `writing` row starting after the two weeks the plan writes ahead: say the lessons the plan teaches it (`plannedLessons`, about that many) and when it starts (`nextDate`), not that they're on the way. False for every other row

cadence.description: When an exam's written tests (an essay, a discursive test) are practiced: weekly (the default, spaced practice), biweekly (every other week and the final stretch) or finalWeeks (only the final weeks before the exam, which needs a date). The total practice stays the same

fullCourse.description: true: study everything, even after the exam. Until the exam the plan stays the one its date shapes (what the exam asks most first, mocks, the final stretch); what doesn't fit before it goes on after the exam at the learner's time. false: the plan ends at the exam and leaves out what doesn't fit. Exams only: other goals study everything by having no date (`setTargetDate` with null)

choice.description: deep: every lesson of it, core and depth, with the time what the plan keeps leaves. essential: its core, the first third of its lessons, before what builds on it (the default). quick: one short lesson that sums it up with a worked example. skip: none of it; what builds on it no longer waits for it, and its own topics leave the plan unless another skill teaches them. No choice ever pushes out a topic its core keeps

oneOf.description: How to study some of the plan's bases (`bases`: the skills its topics or final work build on, worth less to the goal than what builds on them). Bases not named keep their choice

Brings in the lessons the learner's own time fits by the plan's date, at the time, date and pace their plan has: the plan is planned again from today as a change of theirs plans it, so topics its date left out, or more depth, come in where they fit. The plan offers it as `fitOffer` (GET /v1/goals/{goalId}/plan) when it adds lessons

areas.description: Area names exactly as the plan lists them

start.description: pastBasics: these areas start past their foundations, at their higher bands (the learner said their lessons are too basic). basics: they start from their foundations again

name.description: The part as the learner says it, such as biology and chemistry

skillIds.description: The area's skills in the part, from the plan's graph

dailyMinutes.description: Minutes a day for this goal

details.description: What onboarding understood: exam, date, target score, course or position, level, reason, purpose, role

language.description: The language the learner studies in

targetDate.description: A new goal's deadline: from tomorrow through calendar day 3,650 after the learner's today, inclusive. A date outside either bound is refused with 422 TARGET_DATE_OUT_OF_RANGE before any goal is created.

bearerAuth.description: Zoonk session token sent in the Authorization header.
